title: Staggered fintech adoption on loan default rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with unit and period fixed effects (TWFE).
- Why: The data are panel with banks (units) observed over time, and all treated banks belong to a single adoption cohort (simplified staggered adoption), so a standard DiD with bank and time fixed effects consistently estimates the average treatment effect on the treated under parallel trends. In real staggered multi-cohort settings, estimators like Callaway–Sant’Anna or Sun–Abraham would be preferred; here the “single-cohort” simplification justifies TWFE.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of fintech adoption, treated and never-treated banks would have followed parallel trends in default rates.
  - No anticipatory effects: Banks do not change behavior before adoption in expectation of treatment.
  - Stable composition and SUTVA: No compositional changes correlated with treatment; no spillovers across banks.
  - Correct timing: Post equals 1 only after the adoption period for the treated cohort.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Packages -----------------------------------------------------------------
pkgs <- c("data.table", "fixest")
to_install <- pkgs[!sapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if(length(to_install) > 0) install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")

library(data.table)
library(fixest)

# Data ---------------------------------------------------------------------
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s08_data.csv"
dt <- fread(path)

# Basic checks
stopifnot(all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(dt)))
# Ensure expected types
dt[, `:=`(
  unit_id = as.integer(unit_id),
  period  = as.integer(period),
  treated = as.integer(treated),
  post    = as.integer(post),
  treat_x_post = as.integer(treat_x_post),
  y = as.numeric(y)
)]

# Main DiD: TWFE with bank and period fixed effects, clustered SEs ----------
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)

# Extract and print the main effect
ct <- coeftable(m_twfe)
beta  <- ct["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
se    <- ct["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
tval  <- ct["treat_x_post", "t value"]
pval  <- ct["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
ci    <- confint(m_twfe, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)

cat("\n===== Main DiD Estimate (TWFE; clustered by bank) =====\n")
cat(sprintf("Coefficient on treat_x_post: %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("Std. Error: %.4f | t: %.2f | p-value: %.4f\n", se, tval, pval))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci[1], ci[2]))
cat("Interpretation: Change in loan default rate (in absolute units; e.g., -0.0500 = -5 percentage points).\n")

# Robustness 1: Two-way clustered SEs (bank and period) --------------------
m_twfe_2c <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id + period)
ct2 <- coeftable(m_twfe_2c)
beta2  <- ct2["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]
se2    <- ct2["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
pval2  <- ct2["treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
ci2    <- confint(m_twfe_2c, "treat_x_post", level = 0.95)

cat("\n===== Robustness: Two-way clustered SEs (bank & period) =====\n")
cat(sprintf("Coefficient on treat_x_post: %.4f\n", beta2))
cat(sprintf("Std. Error: %.4f | p-value: %.4f\n", se2, pval2))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci2[1], ci2[2]))

# Robustness 2: Manual 2x2 DiD using group-time means ----------------------
# Using pre/post as defined in the data (post == 0 vs 1)
means <- dt[, .(
  mt_post  = mean(y[treated == 1 & post == 1]),
  mt_pre   = mean(y[treated == 1 & post == 0]),
  mc_post  = mean(y[treated == 0 & post == 1]),
  mc_pre   = mean(y[treated == 0 & post == 0])
)]
did_manual <- with(means, (mt_post - mt_pre) - (mc_post - mc_pre))

cat("\n===== Robustness: Manual 2x2 DiD (difference of means) =====\n")
cat(sprintf("Manual DiD estimate: %.4f\n", did_manual))

# Robustness 3: Event-study dynamics (single-cohort assumption) ------------
# Assume adoption occurs at period 4 for treated cohort; build relative time.
# rel_time = 0 at adoption, -1 just before adoption, etc.
dt[, rel_time := period - 4L]

# Event-study with unit and period FE; reference period is -1 (the last pre period).
m_es <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~ unit_id)

# Extract dynamic effects
es_coef <- coef(m_es)
es_se   <- sqrt(diag(vcov(m_es)))
keep_idx <- grepl("^rel_time::", names(es_coef)) & grepl("#treated$", names(es_coef))
dyn <- data.table(term = names(es_coef)[keep_idx],
                  beta = es_coef[keep_idx],
                  se   = es_se[keep_idx])
# Parse relative time from term labels
dyn[, rel := as.integer(sub("rel_time::\\(([-]?[0-9]+)\\)#treated", "\\1", term))]

setorder(dyn, rel)

cat("\n===== Event-study (unit & period FE; ref = -1) =====\n")
cat("Relative-time effects for treated vs control (beta [se]):\n")
for(i in seq_len(nrow(dyn))) {
  cat(sprintf("  rel_time = %2d:  %.4f  [%.4f]\n", dyn$rel[i], dyn$beta[i], dyn$se[i]))
}

# Simple pre-trend check: list pre-period betas (<= -2)
pre_dyn <- dyn[rel <= -2]
if(nrow(pre_dyn) > 0){
  avg_abs_pre <- mean(abs(pre_dyn$beta))
  cat("\nPre-trend diagnostic: average absolute pre-period effect (rel <= -2)\n")
  cat(sprintf("  Mean |beta| (pre): %.4f\n", avg_abs_pre))
} else {
  cat("\nPre-trend diagnostic: not enough pre-periods beyond the reference to assess trends.\n")
}

cat("\nAnalysis complete.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Algorithmic credit scoring should improve screening and monitoring, reducing the share of marginal/high-risk loans and thus lowering default rates at adopting banks relative to never-adopters.
- Magnitude: Approximately −3 to −8 percentage points (−0.03 to −0.08) on the default-rate scale, depending on the baseline default rate and adoption intensity. A midpoint around −5 percentage points is plausible in this stylized setting. The event-study should show near-zero pre-trends and sustained negative post-adoption effects.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Staggered DID (Callaway-Sant'Anna or Sun-Abraham) — cohort-specific ATTs; treatment=fintech adoption
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Fintech-adopting banks reduce default rates relative to non-adopters
